response.headline: The Week in Numbers: Trump goes nuclear, TikTok sells up
response.summary: STORY: From how Trump Media went nuclear, to TikTok's big U.S. sale...This is the Week in Numbers.:: Week in Numbers:: $6 billion$6 billion was the value of an unusual merger between President Donald Trump's social media company and a nuclear fusion firm.It will see a tie-up between Trump Media and Google-backed TAE Technologies.It came just days after fusion industry leaders asked for more federal funding from the U.S. Energy Department.Peter Loge leads the Project on Ethics in Political Communication at The George Washington University."Any time a member of the president's family's name is on a commercial enterprise, it raises ethical questions. Are people buying the thing because the president's name is on it? Are people buying Trump branded products because they think it'll help him get close to the president or that the president will like them more?":: 80%Just over 80% of TikTok's U.S. business will be sold to avoid a ban in the country.Chinese owner ByteDance said it had signed a binding agreement with three major investors: Oracle, Silver Lake and Abu Dhabi-based MGX.The deal will build a new U.S. company called TikTok USDS Joint Venture, with ByteDance holding just under a fifth of it.:: 0.75%0.75% is the new benchmark interest rate in Japan - up from a previous 0.5%.It's the highest number seen in three decades, and the Bank of Japan showed a readiness for further hikes.Policymakers also removed language that growth and price rises will stagnate due to higher U.S. tariffs.Which showed their belief the country is on course to hit its 2% inflation target.:: $19.5 billion$19.5 billion is the writedown taken by Ford as it does a big rethink on electric cars. The auto giant killed several models and said it would pivot to gas and hybrid models. Its move comes after demand for EVs fell in the U.S., where the Trump administration has pulled incentives for buyers. :: $108.4 billionAnd $108.4 billion was the hostile bid Warner Bros Discovery turned down from Paramount Skydance. Warner's board argued Paramount's offer misled shareholders over its financing. It argued the offer was 'inferior' to a merger agreement it already had in place with Netflix.Whoever wins the bidding war will get hold of popular film franchises like 'Harry Potter' and 'DC Comics'.
